title: feat(scripts): gate a test source naming a changeset the tree carries (objectui#9583)
body:
Fixes #9583

## What changed

A new gate, `scripts/check-pending-changeset-literals.mjs`, holds the rule the card states: **a test's source may not name a file `.changeset/` currently carries.**

- `scripts/check-pending-changeset-literals.mjs` — the gate. `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals` is the human entry point.
- `scripts/__tests__/check-pending-changeset-literals.test.ts` — the pins, and the blocking copy: it runs the gate over the real tree.
- `scripts/__tests__/dollar-dialect-alias-census.test.ts` — the one occurrence the gate found on this tree, repaired.
- `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs` — one ledger entry for the new suite (it names three permanent documents as arguments to a path predicate and opens none of them).

## Measurement first — the reading that shaped the gate

Asked of the tree before anything was written, over the literals `deriveCandidates()` resolves out of all 99 test sources it scans:

| test source | document it names | pending? |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `check-changeset-claims.test.ts` | `.changeset/README.md` | no — documentation, survives every release |
| `check-changeset-overwrite.test.ts` | `.changeset/README.md` | no |
| `check-changeset-presence.test.ts` | `.changeset/README.md` | no |
| `dollar-dialect-alias-census.test.ts` | `.changeset/8447-valuedatasource-dollar-operator-refusal.md` | **yes** |

⇒ **one** live occurrence, plus three legitimate `README.md` namings that the gate must not report. The control that says this reading discriminates rather than being a scanner that resolved nothing: the same instrument, same population, separates those two classes — and the fixture suite carries a FIRING CONTROL beside every empty answer, for the same reason.

The repair is in this change because a gate that cannot be green cannot land. It is the mechanical form objectui#9582 already pinned: `roleOf` routes by path PREFIX, so the basename carries no meaning and a synthetic name serves the assertion identically.

## Why the literals come from the existing scanner

The hazard runs **through** `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs`: that scanner resolves markdown path literals out of test sources and offers only the ones that EXIST, so a literal naming a pending declaration becomes a ledger entry — and `pnpm changeset:version` deletes exactly those files. A literal the scanner cannot resolve never becomes an entry and so can never go stale.

So the gate asks that scanner rather than growing a second one. It is then the pre-version image of the very instrument that reds post-version, and the two cannot drift apart. A re-implementation would have to be kept equal by hand, and the day it stopped being equal the gate would go quiet while the release lane kept failing.

## The gate's self-description is the deliverable, so here is what it refuses to claim

Written into the file's own header, not only here:

- ⛔ It does **not** claim every finding would red `Validate the post-version tree` today. A document covered by a ledger CLASS entry (`.changeset/**`) produces no audit finding when the file disappears. The rule is still the rule, because that absorption is a property of the ledger line beside the test, not of the test, and it can change without the test being touched. A gate that asked the narrower question would go quiet the moment somebody re-adjudicated a test for unrelated reasons.
- ⛔ It does **not** see a name that is not in `.changeset/` today. The two fixture literals the card names in `check-changeset-overwrite.test.ts` are therefore not findings now; they become findings on the pull request that ADDS a declaration under either name. That is the predicate the hazard itself has.
- ⛔ The scanner's blind spots are the gate's blind spots — a literal inside a comment, built from a variable, or carrying an interpolation. Both of the first two are pinned as declared boundaries, each with a firing control.

## Where it runs, and why no new workflow

Its own test runs it over the real tree, so the ordinary vitest suite is the blocking copy — the placement `check-installed-spec-pin-claims.mjs` and `doc-version-claims.test.ts` already have, and for the same reason: this reads the tree, needs no install, no build and no base ref, so a dedicated workflow would buy a second thing to keep wired and nothing else.

The two pull-request shapes that can make the intersection non-empty both reach that suite, and **neither leg is assumed** — the test reads each one off the file that decides it:

| shape | why the shards run |
|:--|:--|
| a change to a TEST SOURCE | the scan roots are not among `ci.yml`'s `:(exclude,glob)` pathspecs |
| a change that ADDS a declaration | `.changeset/**` IS excluded, and the second stage rescues it: `markdown-test-inputs.mjs` answers that a test reads the path |

If that second answer ever goes empty, the pin reds and somebody reconsiders the gate's home instead of it silently covering one shape instead of two.

## Verification

Commands run in this worktree; the union below was taken at `7333327dc`.

| command | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec vitest run` over the 8 affected `scripts/__tests__` suites | 8 files, 223 tests passed |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` over the 2 further suites naming the edited scanner | 2 files, 27 tests passed |
| `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit` | exit 0 — 100 candidates, all adjudicated; 73 declared entries, all present |
| `node scripts/check-pending-changeset-literals.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — "No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed" |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:entry-guard` / `check:control-bytes` / `check:test-path-roots` / `check:comment-mask-corpus` / `check:new-line-citations` | exit 0 each |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over this diff | NOT GOVERNED — 5 paths checked against 5 surfaces, none matched |
| `pnpm exec eslint . --no-inline-config` | 5020 files; 95 pre-existing errors, all under `apps/` `e2e/` `packages/`, **0 in any file this change touches** |

### Ablation — both legs, from the committed state, restored and proven restored

**1. The predicate can fail.** `isPendingDeclaration` mutated to `return false`, proven on disk by blob hash (`c467fdf` HEAD vs `1809456` on disk) before the run:

```
MUTATED SUITE exit=1      Tests  4 failed | 11 passed (15)
RESTORED SUITE exit=0     Tests  15 passed (15)     git diff HEAD: []
```

**2. The gate catches the real instance.** The repair reverted in place — the real declaration name put back — proven on disk by blob hash before the run:

```
GATE ON MUTATED TREE exit=1
    • scripts/__tests__/dollar-dialect-alias-census.test.ts
        names .changeset/8447-valuedatasource-dollar-operator-refusal.md
GATE ON RESTORED TREE exit=0
```

Both legs carry a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` restore on an absolute path, and both assert restoration by comparing the on-disk blob hash against the HEAD blob rather than by reading an exit code.

### Not measured

`pnpm check:node-esm-load` exits 1 in this container for a reason outside this change: turbo shares one cache across every worktree of the checkout, and it refused two entries on provenance because the build was replayed from a sibling worktree (`/home/user/objectui-issue-9323`). This diff touches no published package, so that gate has nothing to say about it either way. Recorded as NOT MEASURED rather than as a failure.

## Acceptance notes

- **Noted, not filed:** `scripts/__tests__/check-changeset-overwrite.test.ts` still carries two fixture literals (`plum-pandas-wave.md`, `6336-new-work.md`) that are not declarations today. They are already named on #9583's body, so filing again would duplicate it; the gate reports them by name the day either lands, which is what the card asked for instead of another one-at-a-time rename.
- **Noted, not filed:** the shared turbo cache across sibling worktrees makes `check:node-esm-load` refuse entries on provenance. That is a property of this container, not of the repository.
